post.description:
Launches a new inspection run asynchronously.

The session folder and its ``in_progress`` card are created synchronously so
the returned ``inspection_id`` is immediately queryable via
``GET /inspections/{id}``. The actual load + preprocessing + autodetect
work runs in the background; clients poll the GET endpoint to observe the
``status`` transition to ``completed`` or ``failed``.

Request cancellation of an in-progress inspection.

Safe to call on a finished inspection — returns the current status with a
``"job already finished"`` message instead of an error.

delete.description:
Bulk-deletes inspection folders that are empty, dead (orphaned), or exact duplicates.

Inspections with linked trained models are skipped and reported in

individually after the linked models are deleted.

Returns the current schema (PKs, FKs, per-column encoding types).

This is whatever ``inspection_metadata.json`` currently holds — either the
auto-detected values or the user's last edit via ``PUT``. The pristine
auto-detected snapshot is preserved separately in
``autodetected_inspection_metadata.json``. Returns 404 if the inspection is
still ``in_progress`` or ``failed``.

Returns the pristine auto-detected schema captured at inspection time.

Reads ``autodetected_inspection_metadata.json``, the frozen snapshot that is
written once when the inspection runs and is never overwritten by user
edits. Used by the UI's "reset to autodetected" action.

post.description:
Defines logical rules for a completed inspection.

Builds and stores the rule manager using the inspection metadata and
the resolved rules configuration.

get.description:
Return the rules YAML snapshot captured at inspection time.

This is the exact ``rules.yaml`` content used to preprocess the dataset,
independent of any later edits to the live config. Returns 404 when the
snapshot does not exist (older inspections, or run before snapshotting
was added).

Evaluate each logical rule in the live rules.yaml against the inspection's real data.

Returns per-rule compliance: how many rows satisfy the rule vs. total checked.
Only rules whose types can be evaluated on pre-PRE data are included
(inequality and FK rules). Derived rules are skipped — they produce columns
that don't exist in the original dataset.

``sample_size`` caps rows per table before running checks.

put.description:
Overwrites only the ``relationships`` section of ``inspection_metadata.json``.

The encoding-types section is preserved untouched. Training consumes the merged
metadata file, so edits here take effect on the next training run.

Overwrites only the ``encoding_types`` section of ``inspection_metadata.json``.

The relationships section is preserved untouched. Training consumes the merged
metadata file, so edits here take effect on the next training run.

Set the **non-destructive** training-time exclusion list.

Unlike ``PUT /autodetect/excluded-columns`` (which physically drops columns
from the cached parquet), this only records which columns training should
skip. The data stays on disk and the column remains in ``encoding_types``,
so the choice is fully reversible — this is how the user opts a flagged
column back in (by removing it from the list).

Set the **Reglas de negocio (BRC) phase** column-drop list.

Stored separately from ``excluded_columns`` (the Carga de Datos list) so a
drop chosen for one rule set never leaks back into Carga de Datos or into a
different rule set on the same upload. These columns stay in the cached
parquet and are dropped (unioned with ``excluded_columns``) only when a BRC
run materialises. Fully reversible.

Remove specific columns from an inspection's metadata **and** from the cached
processed parquet files in a single atomic operation.

Use this endpoint (instead of the generic ``PUT /autodetect/encoding-types``) when
the user explicitly excludes columns post-inspection, so that the cached data and
the schema stay in sync. Excluded columns are:

* Removed from ``encoding_types`` in ``inspection_metadata.json``.
* Removed from any FK/PK relationships that reference them.
* Physically dropped from the matching ``processed_data/<table>.parquet`` files.

The changes are irreversible on disk; use "Restaurar autodetectado" only for the
schema — the parquet files are not restored by that action.

does not return ``409`` for linked artifacts — cascading is the point.

no longer present on disk are silently skipped.

environment (or has 'mostlyai' in its command line) but is NOT the

Autodetect.title: Autodetect
Autodetect.description:
Contents of ``inspection_metadata.json`` — the editable source of truth
for an inspection's schema.

``encoding_types`` maps ``table -> column -> type`` where type is one of
the MostlyAI labels (``TABULAR_NUMERIC_AUTO``, ``TABULAR_CATEGORICAL``,
``TABULAR_DATETIME``, ``TABULAR_CHARACTER``, ...).

``warnings`` lists columns the inspection flagged and excluded by default
(the user can keep them via ``force_include_columns``).

inspection_id.title: Inspection Id
inspection_id.description: Source upload (inspection) id whose preprocessed data is the input.

name.title: Name
name.description: Optional human-readable name for this run.

rules_config_path.title: Rules Config Path
rules_config_path.description: Override for the rules YAML path; when null, the server resolves the current ``rules`` config (override if present, else default).

enable_profiling.title: Enable Profiling
enable_profiling.description: Whether to generate ydata-profiling reports for the new columns.

BRCRuleWarning.title: BRCRuleWarning
BRCRuleWarning.description: Advisory raised while loading or applying a rule during the BRC run.

BRCSummary.title: BRCSummary
BRCSummary.description: Catalogue entry for a BRC run.

CategoricalCondition.title: CategoricalCondition
CategoricalCondition.description:
Force a column to follow target proportions over categorical values.

``weights`` are relative — they need not sum to 100; the server normalizes
them and allocates rows proportionally.

ColumnWarning.title: ColumnWarning
ColumnWarning.description:
A per-column issue surfaced during inspection (e.g. an incompatible
numeric/text mix recommended for exclusion).

``default_excluded`` signals the frontend to pre-select the column for
exclusion in the type-detection view; the user can toggle it back on.

table.title: Table
table.description: Target subject table. Defaults to the first subject table when omitted.

ConditionalConfig.title: ConditionalConfig
ConditionalConfig.description: Conditional-generation spec: per-column constraints applied to one table.

ConfigBulkResult.title: ConfigBulkResult
ConfigBulkResult.description: Response for bulk config operations (bootstrap / clean / reset).

ConfigContent.title: ConfigContent
ConfigContent.description: Full content payload for a single config, returned by ``GET /configs/{id}``.

ConfigFile.title: ConfigFile
ConfigFile.description:
A config file available for the frontend to list/edit.

``id`` is the relative path of the real file under ``backend/config/``
(e.g. ``rules.yaml``, ``pipelines/example_pipeline.yaml``). Pass it
directly to the ``GET/PUT/DELETE /configs/{id}`` endpoints — friendly
aliases like ``rules`` or ``mostly_ai`` are accepted there too, but the
id returned here is always the canonical path form.

``exists`` is ``True`` when the real ``*.yaml`` file has been created
(by ``make config`` or by editing through the API). When ``False``, the
user still needs to bootstrap the file from its ``*.example.yaml``
template.

ConfigScope.title: ConfigScope
ConfigScope.description:
Category label used to group config files in the API.

- It answers: "what functional area does this config belong to?"

Folder-based mapping used by the backend classifier:
- ``all``:
  include every supported config file under ``backend/config/``.
- ``pipeline``:
  include pipeline-level config files under ``backend/config/pipelines/``
  except the dedicated rules subfolder.
- ``evaluation``:
  include ``evaluation.yaml`` (and any future evaluation-focused files).
- ``rules``:
  include global rules files (for example ``rules.yaml`` / ``rules.py``)
  and pipeline-specific rules under ``backend/config/pipelines/rules/``.

Practical reason this enum exists:
- ``GET /configs?scope=...`` needs a canonical filter value.
- ``ConfigFile.scope`` and ``ConfigContent.scope`` need a consistent,
  machine-readable grouping shared by frontend and backend.

DataFile.title: DataFile
DataFile.description:
A data file available under ``backend/data/``.

The API exposes this so the frontend can let the user pick input files
without having to know absolute server-side paths (which differ between
Docker and local runs).

DateRangeCondition.title: DateRangeCondition
DateRangeCondition.description:
Synthesize a datetime column with values drawn uniformly between dates.

``start`` and ``end`` are ISO date/datetime strings. Setting them equal
pins the column to a single date.

DeletedPipeline.title: DeletedPipeline

DeletedSimulation.title: DeletedSimulation
DeletedSimulation.description: Confirmation returned after successfully deleting a simulation.

EngineInfo.title: EngineInfo
EngineInfo.description:
One available synthesis engine.

Attributes:
    name: Stable engine identifier (the value to pass when selecting it).
    label: Human-friendly name for display.
    config_id: Settings-config alias whose schema (see
        ``GET /configs/schemas``) describes this engine's model settings.
    mode_presets_id: Presets-config alias, or ``None`` if the engine has no
        mode presets.
    has_mode_presets: Convenience flag, ``True`` when ``mode_presets_id`` is
        set.

EnginesResponse.description:
Response for ``GET /engines``.

Attributes:
    default: Engine name the application uses when none is explicitly chosen.
    engines: All registered engines.

FixedCondition.title: FixedCondition
FixedCondition.description: Force a column to a single constant value on every generated row.

FixedTargetConfig.title: FixedTargetConfig
FixedTargetConfig.description:
Hold one table at an exact (rule-compliant) row count, letting the rest float.

The engine only honors sizes on subject tables; context children always
cascade from their parent. To enforce a child table's row count the server
oversimulates the mother table adaptively (re-estimating the child-per-mother
yield each attempt) until ``table`` reaches ``rows`` compliant rows, then
trims the overflow. The mother and the remaining tables end up with whatever
size that requires. Runs with or without rejection-sampling rules; when rules
exist, only compliant rows count toward ``rows``.

composite_pks.title: Composite Pks
composite_pks.description: Optional per-table composite primary keys (table name → list of column names). For each listed table the inspector synthesizes a single unique PK column by concatenating the named columns, instead of relying on heuristic single-column PK detection. Use for datasets whose natural key spans several columns (e.g. patient_id + year). Falls back to heuristics if the named columns are missing or do not form a unique key. An empty list (``"TABLE": []``) requests a surrogate row-index key — use it for event-style tables with no natural unique key.

excluded_columns.title: Excluded Columns
excluded_columns.description: Optional per-table column exclusion list (table name → list of column names). Listed columns are stripped from the autodetect metadata and the cached preprocessed data after the inspection run, so they are invisible to training and all downstream pipeline steps.

JobProgress.title: JobProgress
JobProgress.description:
Coarse progress indicator written by long-running flows.

``step`` counts phases COMPLETED so far (0..total). ``label`` describes
the phase currently in progress. Surfaced only while the owning job's
``status`` is ``in_progress``; once it flips to ``completed`` the field
is no longer relevant.

ModelSummary.description: Summary of a trained model returned by the catalog.

ModelTrainingConfig.title: ModelTrainingConfig
ModelTrainingConfig.description:
The Mostly AI config a model was trained with.

Surfaced by ``GET /models/{model_id}/config`` so the UI can show the full
configuration the run was launched with. ``config`` is the verbatim
(override-merged) ``mostly_config.json`` content — an empty object when the
config was never archived for that run.

NumericCondition.title: NumericCondition
NumericCondition.description:
Synthesize a numeric column with a parameterized generator.

``uniform`` draws values evenly in ``[min, max]``. ``normal`` draws from a
Gaussian with the given ``mean``/``std``, clamped to ``[min, max]``.

The ``PipelineTracker`` copies the launched YAML and freezes a small set of

fetches this so users can inspect what actually ran without opening files
on the server.

RejectionSamplingReport.title: RejectionSamplingReport
RejectionSamplingReport.description:
How rejection sampling performed during a simulation run.

Written by ``SimulationTracker.save_rejection_sampling_report`` only when at
least one rejection-sampling rule applied. ``attempts`` is how many
generate/filter passes ran (capped at ``max_attempts``); ``partial_results``
is ``True`` when the cap was hit before reaching the subject target or a
child table's proportional compliance target.

Subjects are held at exactly their requested size; ``child_targets`` are the
proportional (real child:subject ratio × subject size) compliance goals the
engine cannot enforce directly — rejection sampling retries up to
``max_attempts`` to close the gap and reports how far it got via the per-table
``accepted`` counts.

RejectionSamplingTableStats.title: RejectionSamplingTableStats
RejectionSamplingTableStats.description:
Per-table counts from rejection sampling.

``rejected`` counts rows discarded for *failing the rule* (the compliance
signal). ``trimmed`` counts compliant rows discarded only as overflow — i.e.
rows of subjects not kept by best-subset selection (and their children), so
the two are not conflated.

SanityReport.title: SanityReport
SanityReport.description: Sanity-checks report for a simulation run.

SanityReportRow.title: SanityReportRow
SanityReportRow.description:
One entry from a simulation's sanity-checks report.

Mirrors the unified schema produced by `_build_general_sanity_check_row`
and `RuleManager.run_rules_sanity_checks`. ``type`` is ``"rule"`` for
logical-rule checks and ``"general"`` for structural ones (referential
integrity, contextual FK consistency).

For ``type="rule"`` rows the identity fields (``origin_col``,
``target_col``, etc.) allow the frontend to reconstruct the same label
the rules banner shows, so each row maps unambiguously to one yaml rule.

name.title: Name
name.description: Optional human-readable name for this generation run.

model_id.title: Model Id
model_id.description: ID of the trained model to simulate from.

sample_size.title: Sample Size
sample_size.description: Number of synthetic records to generate. Uses model default when omitted.

synthetic_data_file_format.title: Synthetic Data File Format
synthetic_data_file_format.description: Synthetic output table format for this simulation run.

table_sample_sizes.title: Table Sample Sizes
table_sample_sizes.description: Per-table row-count overrides. Only honored for subject tables (those without a context foreign key); Mostly AI cascades counts for context children from their parent, so entries targeting children are accepted but ignored with a server-side warning. Falls back to `sample_size` for subject tables not listed here.

conditional.description: Conditional-generation spec. Builds a `sample_seed` table that fixes or steers selected columns (constant value, target proportions, or a numeric generator) so generation is conditioned on them.

max_attempts.title: Max Attempts
max_attempts.description: Max generate/filter passes for rejection or fixed-target sampling. Overrides the rules.yaml value. Each retry restarts the engine, which is far slower than drawing a bigger batch — prefer raising `overgenerate_factor` over this.

overgenerate_factor.title: Overgenerate Factor
overgenerate_factor.description: Overgeneration multiplier applied to each sampling draw. Overrides the rules.yaml value. Cheaper than retries: one larger batch beats another engine round-trip.

fixed_target.description: Enforce an exact row count on one table (typically a context child) instead of on the mother table. The mother is oversimulated until the target table reaches the requested compliant rows; all other tables are left to whatever size that requires. Mutually exclusive with `sample_size` and `table_sample_sizes`.
